entities.name: Marcus Ummidius Quadratus Annianus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Ummidius Quadratus Annianus (c. 138–182 CE) was a distinguished Roman Senator whose life was inextricably linked to the highest echelons of the Antonine dynasty, ultimately culminating in a dramatic and fatal involvement in imperial court intrigue. Born into one of Rome's most prominent senatorial families, he was the son of Ummidius Quadratus and Annia Cornificia Faustina, making him a nephew to the Emperor Marcus Aurelius and a first cousin to the future Emperor Commodus. His lineage provided him with a privileged position within the Roman political landscape, marked by a rapid ascent through the cursus honorum typical of imperial relatives, yet it also placed him perilously close to the dangerous currents of power struggles.

Quadratus Annianus's career saw him hold significant offices, including quaestor, praetor, and eventually consul ordinarius in 167 CE, alongside Lucius Verus, co-emperor with Marcus Aurelius. His administrative experience further extended to governing the strategically vital province of Africa as proconsul around 172 CE, a testament to his perceived competence and trustworthiness within the imperial administration. However, his life took a tragic turn when he became embroiled in an unsuccessful plot in 182 CE to assassinate his cousin, the young and increasingly autocratic Emperor Commodus. This conspiracy was instigated primarily by his sister, Lucilla, the emperor's elder sister and former empress, who felt her influence waning under Commodus's erratic rule.
